constellations.name: At Work
constellations.subtitle: The day job
constellations.blurb: The day job: automations, analyses, maps and data audits that keep a food bank's partner network accurate and help feed two-thirds of Arizona.

constellations.subtitle: Reverse engineering & mods
constellations.blurb: The Saints Row (2006) engine, reverse-engineered into 48 research reports — then a map editor, a character creator, mods and a Mac port.

constellations.subtitle: Contributions to other projects
constellations.blurb: Pull requests to other people's projects: co-op multiplayer for a Saints Row revival, and GPU and reliability fixes for a suite of open-source Rust creative apps.

constellations.name: Markets & Finance
constellations.subtitle: Backtests, dashboards & calculators
constellations.blurb: Questions about money answered with real history instead of hunches.

constellations.name: Pokémon GO
constellations.subtitle: Community & data
constellations.blurb: Running a local Pokémon GO community turned into data projects: dashboards, maps, generators and a Discord relay.

constellations.name: Apps
constellations.subtitle: iPhone & web apps
constellations.blurb: Full apps that run on an iPhone: a household planner that AI assistants can help run, and a 4X strategy game against 249 AI commanders.

constellations.name: Tools & Experiments
constellations.subtitle: Utilities, ports & hacks
constellations.blurb: Small tools and deep dives: an image combiner, a browser extension, old games ported to Apple Silicon, a PSP audio streamer and an early data notebook.

projects.name: AZFoodHelp Inquiry Automation
projects.description: A 6-phase Power Automate system that routes every AZFoodHelp.org inquiry to the right team, logs it, and reports on it in a live Power BI dashboard.

caseStudy.why: Contact-form emails for AZFoodHelp.org were sorted by hand. The goal: route every inquiry to the right team automatically, measure how fast each gets answered, and show it all live — without a minute of downtime while it was built.
highlights: Keyword classifier built from 897 historical submissions, routing 10 categories (Home Delivery, Volunteers, Food Donations, Finance, Partnerships…)
Three flow versions iterated with the previous one still live, so routing never went down
12-column SharePoint intake log: Arizona-time timestamps, response times, and a quality flag with manual override
Power BI dashboard with 5 KPI cards and 8× daily scheduled refresh — manual email handling dropped to near zero
caseStudy.learned: Simple beats clever. One long chain of nested conditions kept breaking; splitting it into plain steps made it reliable and easy to explain.

projects.name: Grocery Rescue Network Map
projects.description: A multi-layer ArcGIS map of agencies, donors and grocery-rescue partners across 76,000 square miles — and a visual case for grants: who can store food, who can't, and where capacity would grow the network.

caseStudy.why: The food resourcing team needs one picture for two jobs: deciding where to source food, and showing funders why a grant matters. That means seeing where partners are, what each can store, and where the need is that no partner reaches yet.
highlights: Layers agency locations, food donor sites, grocery-rescue partners and Feeding America opportunity data
Shows which partners have cold, frozen or dry storage — and which have none — so a grant request can point to specific gaps
Heat map of zip-code-level web inquiries over agency coverage, surfacing high-need areas with no nearby service
Turns 'where should capacity go next?' into a map the team can put in front of funders and leadership
caseStudy.learned: A map turns 'we think there's a gap' into a place a funder can point at.

projects.name: Federal Shutdown Impact Map
projects.description: Built during the federal government shutdown: an ArcGIS map of where affected federal workers are, how many at each location, and the closest agency partners — so the food bank knew where to send additional resources.

caseStudy.why: When the federal government shut down, federal workers went without pay and the food bank needed to know where that need would land. The question: who is affected, where are they, and which agency partners are closest?
highlights: Mapped the federal locations whose staff would be affected by the shutdown
Showed how many people work at each location
Layered in the closest agency partners to each site
Pointed to where additional resources needed to go
caseStudy.learned: In a fast-moving crisis, a map answers 'where do we send help?' faster than any spreadsheet.

projects.name: ERP Migration Audit
projects.description: Owned the agency data sheet for an ERP migration end to end: built the document, pulled the data, made sure every field was filled and captured, and fielded the questions.

caseStudy.why: An ERP migration is only as good as the data that goes into it. The agency records needed one clean, complete, agreed structure before user acceptance testing — and someone to own it from template to sign-off.
highlights: Created the document: worked with stakeholders to identify every required column and structured it to management's spec
Pulled the data: researched and populated values from existing agency records
Checked completeness: audited the sheet so every required field was filled and captured before UAT
Fielded questions: point of contact after distribution for field values, data expectations and entry rules
caseStudy.learned: Before moving any data, everyone has to agree on what each field means. Most problems came from that, not from the data itself.

projects.name: Households-to-Pounds Analysis
projects.description: Are agency partners overserving, underserving or just right? Stitched a year of distribution reports and a full agency poundage report into one dataset with an agency ID key, then built an interactive dashboard for stakeholders.

caseStudy.why: Pounds distributed only mean something next to the households they reach. The question was whether each agency partner is overserving, underserving or just right — and the answer was spread across a year of distribution reports plus one very large poundage report.
highlights: Stitched 24 reports from across the year tracking agency distributions
Joined them with a large report of all agency poundage
Built an agency ID key so every partner lines up from report to report
Compared households served to pounds received to classify each partner as overserving, underserving or just right
Interactive dashboard so stakeholders can explore the results themselves
caseStudy.learned: Giving every agency one shared ID was the boring step, and it's what let two dozen separate reports line up.

projects.name: Link2Feed System Audit
projects.description: After the ERP switch, the Link2Feed neighbor database still carried old-system IDs, addresses and contacts. Reconciled Link2Feed against NetSuite and updated every agency card in the network by hand.

caseStudy.why: Agency partners log every neighbor visit in Link2Feed. After the move to the new ERP, its agency records still matched the old system — old IDs, outdated addresses and contacts — so they no longer lined up with NetSuite.
highlights: Exported all Link2Feed agency data and all NetSuite agency data
Synthesized the two to find mismatched IDs, addresses and contacts
Updated every agency card in the network manually so both systems agree
caseStudy.learned: A migration isn't finished at the ERP — every system that points at it needs cleaning up too.

projects.name: Appointment Plan Audit
projects.description: After the ERP switch, pallet counts on some appointment plans — but not all — had been doubled to work around a pallet-volume rounding issue, which hid what agencies actually receive. Exported every plan, worked through each with its rep and Transportation, then imported 1,200+ corrections.

caseStudy.why: The new ERP rounded pallet volumes in a way that didn't match real distributions, and doubling pallet counts on some plans had been tried as a workaround. Because only some plans were changed, there was no blanket fix — and the actual distribution amounts for each agency were no longer clear.
highlights: Exported every appointment plan in the system
Worked out which plans had doubled counts and which didn't — a plan-by-plan check, not a blanket undo
Sat with each rep to understand their caseload
Met with Transportation to approve and confirm the changes
Imported 1,200+ updates manually
caseStudy.learned: Data that several teams rely on only stays fixed when every team signs off on the change.

projects.name: Vivery Data Audit
projects.description: Vivery powers the find-food-near-you search on AZFoodHelp, but no one was managing its accuracy. Pulled all of it through the API and audited every organization, location and program in a three-level hierarchy.

caseStudy.why: Neighbors use Vivery on AZFoodHelp to find the closest food pantry instead of hunting for one. The system had been left undermanaged — no one owned updates or accuracy.
highlights: Exported all system data through an API pull
Built a three-level hierarchy spreadsheet to audit every organization, location and program
Corrected stale records and added new agency sites across the 76,000-square-mile service area
caseStudy.learned: A public directory needs an owner — accuracy starts slipping the moment nobody's checking.

projects.name: Vivery API Connector
projects.description: The first direct connection to Vivery's API we'd ever set up. A flow on the free tier of Power Automate pulls an organization's full agency data on demand. It's now shared with Vivery to offer to partner food banks across the US.

caseStudy.why: The food bank had used Vivery for years, but every audit started with manual exports. A direct API pull makes the whole network's agency data one click away, with no paid connectors.
highlights: Built on the free tier of Power Automate, so any organization can run it at no cost
Pulls every agency's locations, distribution hours, programs, claimed status and other agency-level fields
Paired with a Python script that writes the same pull to a local folder, ready to audit
Handed both to the Vivery team to share with the food banking organizations they partner with nationwide
caseStudy.learned: When a tool is easy for someone else to run, it can help far more people than the team it was built for.

projects.name: Vivery Claim Outreach
projects.description: Turned a weekly manual export-and-flyer job into a Friday automation. It finds unclaimed Vivery locations, matches each to its agency advocate in the ERP and emails them a ready-to-use outreach packet.

caseStudy.why: Vivery helps neighbors find the closest food pantry instead of driving to a distant one. It works best when each agency claims and manages its own listing. Chasing unclaimed listings used to be a manual job every week: export, filter, then make flyers for each advocate's caseload.
highlights: Runs every Friday: pulls claim status from the Vivery API and checks it against ERP agency data to find the responsible advocate
Emails each advocate only their unclaimed locations, with phone, email and the claim link or code
Attaches a flyer customized to each location, explaining what Vivery is and why the food bank uses it
Monday and Wednesday check-ins track new claims, and locations started claiming within days of the first send
caseStudy.learned: Automating the report wasn't enough on its own. Sending each advocate only their own list is what got locations claimed.

projects.name: SR1 Map Studio
projects.description: Build Saints Row 1 multiplayer maps in the browser, then press Install in game and play them in Saints Reborn.

caseStudy.why: Saints Row (2006) never had a map editor. Map Studio is one — in the browser, with nothing to install — and it exports straight into the running game.
highlights: Map wizard: 9 settings × 10 layouts, previewed from above, always fair for both teams
57 ready-made maps sized like the retail ones, and ~670 placeable pieces
Walk-in rooms, real textures, photo-to-building and graffiti tagging
Built on 48 research reports into the engine's formats
caseStudy.learned: Figuring out the game's file formats took the longest. Once that was done, building an easy editor on top was the fun part.

projects.name: SR1 Creator
projects.description: The Saints Row character creator rebuilt in the browser with the game's real meshes and morphs — plus photo-to-character fitting.

caseStudy.why: The game's character creator, outside the game — so you can design and share a character, or fit one to photos, then enter the values in the real menu.
highlights: Parses the game's packfiles, Xbox 360 textures, meshes and morph targets in the browser — ships no game data
Skin, hair and eye shaders ported from the game's own pixel shaders
Photo fit: 478 face landmarks per photo solve one set of face sliders across several photos
caseStudy.learned: To make characters look right, I had to copy the old game's quirks exactly, even the odd fixes it makes while loading.

projects.name: SR Save Editor
projects.description: Save editor for Saints Reborn on Mac and Windows: cash, weapons, wardrobe, garage, neighbourhoods, homies and the online character.

caseStudy.why: A save editor is the friendliest mod there is — change your story save without touching game files.
highlights: Story save: cash and respect, weapon wheel, wardrobe, garage, crib cache, neighbourhoods and homies
Online character: cash, owned clothing and outfit
Same features on Mac and Windows

projects.name: SR Tweak Menu
projects.description: An in-game cheat menu for Saints Reborn: god mode, wanted level, rocket ammo, vehicle and people spawner, bodyguards, emotes, free camera and more.

caseStudy.why: Every open-world game deserves a trainer you can drive with a controller.
highlights: Opens on F5, or RB + D-pad Down on a controller
God mode, wanted level, rocket and fire ammo, vehicle and people spawner, bodyguards, emotes
Works on the Windows and Mac builds

projects.name: Teleport to Waypoint
projects.description: Drop a waypoint on the map and you're there — on the rooftop, with your car and homies. No more driving across Stilwater.

caseStudy.why: The fun part of Stilwater is rarely the drive to it.
highlights: Lands on the highest surface at the spot — roads, rooftops, the top of the Ultor dome
Your car and homies come with you
Only your own green waypoint triggers it, never a mission marker

projects.name: More Homies
projects.description: Recruit up to 10 homies instead of 3, with all ten heads on the HUD — and bigger gang wars to use them in.

caseStudy.why: The game's party list already held ten followers; the game just never let you fill it.
highlights: Keeps the game's own progression, just with a higher cap
HUD shows all ten follower heads
Experimental entourage mode for up to 30

projects.name: Saints Reborn on Mac
projects.description: Play Saints Row (Xbox 360, 2006) on Apple Silicon Macs: a double-click installer that builds the game from your own disc, plus a mod launcher app.

caseStudy.why: Saints Reborn brought the 360 game to Windows. This brings it to the Mac — free, from your own disc, with no game files in the repo.
highlights: Double-click installer that downloads the free tools and builds the game
Launcher app that opens the mod loader — tick mods, press Play
GPU and frame-rate tuning, with fixes merged back upstream

projects.name: Saints Reborn Co-op
projects.description: Built co-op multiplayer for the Saints Reborn revival of Saints Row: one shared world, story missions every player can finish, and fixes for freezes found by reading the game's own machine code.

caseStudy.about: Saints Reborn is an unofficial Windows port of the original Saints Row, a 2006 open-world crime game that only ever came out on Xbox 360. The game's code is recompiled to run as a normal PC program, not an emulator, and players build it from their own disc. Co-op is a mod on top that lets friends play it together.

highlights.text: Built the shared world: up to 8 players in one city, with a network protocol that turns away mismatched game versions when someone joins
Fixed players who joined a game getting stuck on a black loading screen after a story mission's opening cutscene, so missions now play through for everyone
Fixed whole-game freezes in busy sessions at shops and in fights, by tracing them through the game's disassembly to two deadlocks in how it draws character shadows and clothing

highlights: Five pull requests merged, about 36,000 lines added

projects.name: PhotoCraft
projects.description: Seven merged fixes to an open-source photo editor in Rust: it now survives losing the GPU without losing work, starts almost twice as fast on DX12, and draws correctly on AMD.

caseStudy.about: PhotoCraft is a free, open-source photo editor built from scratch in Rust, a clean-room take on Photoshop. It has layers, masks, adjustment layers, type, brushes and real PSD files, and it runs offline. With over 77,000 stars, it's one of the most-followed creative apps on GitHub. It's part of ArtCraft, a suite of open-source creative apps.

highlights.text: Crash when the GPU disappears (for example, after a driver reset): it now saves unsaved work for recovery and closes cleanly
Slow start-up on Windows DX12: building the GPU pipelines in parallel cut start-up from 13.2 s to 7.3 s
Corrupted canvas on AMD graphics cards using Vulkan: small image levels are now redrawn whole after an edit
Retry GPU after an error now rebuilds the canvas without restarting the app
Smaller fixes: custom shortcuts on Page Up/Page Down work again, an Export As preset survives a damaged preset file, and a broken build

projects.name: FilmCraft
projects.description: Fixes to an open-source video editor in Rust: color grading, timeline edits, export jobs and the automation API.

caseStudy.about: FilmCraft is a free, open-source video editor built from scratch in Rust, for editing, color and sound in the style of Premiere Pro. You cut clips on a timeline, grade color, add effects and export finished video, on Mac, Windows, Linux or in the browser. Scripts and AI assistants can drive it through an automation API.

highlights.text: Color grading: lifting the shadows turned near-black areas into blue specks — fixed
Timeline: moving a clip that was selected twice left one clip on two tracks; the move is now refused
Automation API: applying an effect or starting an export now reports back what happened and where to follow the export

projects.name: VectorCraft
projects.description: Fixes to an open-source vector art tool in Rust: PDF export presets that keep their colors, PDF import that says what it left out, and copies with large images that stay off the clipboard as text.

caseStudy.about: VectorCraft is a free, open-source vector illustration app built from scratch in Rust, in the style of Illustrator. Designers use it for logos, illustrations and print work that scales to any size, then export to PDF and SVG. It runs on Mac, Windows, Linux and in the browser.

highlights.text: PDF export: the Press Quality preset now converts colors to the document's CMYK while keeping their exact values for print
PDF import: tells you when invisible text in the file was left out, instead of dropping it silently
Copy and paste: copying artwork with a large image no longer dumps its whole SVG code onto the clipboard as text

projects.name: EffectCraft
projects.description: GPU fixes to an open-source motion graphics tool in Rust: effects that match the CPU on AMD and Intel, kernels built on first use, and a memory cap sized to the card.

caseStudy.about: EffectCraft is a free, open-source motion graphics and visual effects studio built from scratch in Rust, in the style of After Effects. It layers footage, keyframed animation, 3D cameras and over 300 effects into finished shots, with effects rendered on the GPU.

highlights.text: The Posterize and CC Grid Wipe effects looked different on AMD and Intel graphics cards than on the CPU; they now match
Effects' GPU code is now built the first time each effect is used, one family at a time, instead of all at once
On Linux, the GPU memory limit is sized from the card's actual video memory

projects.name: Craft Anything
projects.description: Windows start-up fixes for the Craft app runtime: when a start can't draw, the next one falls back to a renderer that works.

caseStudy.about: Craft Anything studies how a website, app or game works, then has an AI coding agent build your own version from scratch. It checks the result against the original and keeps refining it. It's the clean-room engine behind the ArtCraft suite.

highlights.text: Windows: when the app can't draw at start-up, the next start falls back to Microsoft's WARP software renderer and opens
A hand-off that ends just before the app is closed now reports its exit, with a Windows test that waits for the launcher
Measured how much idle CPU AMD's Radeon driver uses, and kept the project's notes to exactly the setup that was tested

projects.name: Chronoticker
projects.description: Stock portfolio backtester — simulate any allocation against the S&P 500 with rebalancing & DCA.

caseStudy.why: Would that allocation have beaten the S&P 500? Chronoticker replays portfolio allocations against real history — with rebalancing and dollar-cost averaging — so the answer is a simulation, not a hunch.
highlights: Backtests any allocation against the S&P 500
Models rebalancing strategies and DCA schedules
Charts the full growth path, not just the end number
caseStudy.learned: In money simulations, small rules, like the day a contribution lands, change the result more than you'd expect.

projects.name: Blockwatch
projects.description: Live Bitcoin on-chain dashboard — market, network health, and sentiment, plus comparisons to gold and the national debt.

caseStudy.why: One screen for the Bitcoin questions that used to take five tabs: price, network health, sentiment, and how it all stacks up against gold and the national debt.
highlights: Live market and on-chain data from keyless public APIs (CoinGecko, mempool.space)
Comparisons that give the numbers scale — gold, the US national debt
Fails gracefully when any upstream API is down
caseStudy.learned: Free data sources go down. A good dashboard says when its numbers are out of date instead of passing them off as live.

projects.name: Cashflow Compass
projects.description: See your financial future month by month, up to 3 years ahead — browser-only, with Excel round-trips.

caseStudy.why: Spreadsheets can model your financial future, but they don’t show it. Cashflow Compass projects cashflow month by month, up to three years out — and keeps Excel round-trips working so nobody has to abandon their budget.
highlights: 36-month projection engine running entirely in the browser
Excel import and export via SheetJS — meet budgets where they already live
Projection engine kept separate from the UI, so features land cleanly
caseStudy.learned: Keeping the math separate from the screens made every new feature quicker to add.

projects.name: Project 401k
projects.description: 401(k)-style dollar cost averaging into the S&P 500 — SPY closes, employer match, dividends reinvested.

caseStudy.why: A payroll contribution is the most common investment plan there is, and the hardest to picture. Project 401k replays one against SPY's real closes — your contribution, the employer match, dividends reinvested — and shows what the account would actually be worth.
highlights: Replays contribution schedules against SPY closes back to 1993
Counts the employer match separately from your own money
Reinvests dividends and shows the shares they bought
caseStudy.learned: Leaving dividends out understated a 26-year plan by $165,790 — the honest version needed the data, not a footnote.

projects.name: Calculat-Bur
projects.description: Convert BTC to USD at live prices, then re-price that holding from $50K to $1M — arithmetic, not forecasts.

caseStudy.why: A conversation-settler: what is this BTC holding worth right now, and what would it be worth at $50K to $1M per coin? Arithmetic at live prices — deliberately not forecasts.
highlights: Live BTC pricing via the keyless CoinGecko API
Re-prices a holding across a $50K–$1M range instantly
Forecast-free on purpose: it’s a calculator, not a crystal ball
caseStudy.learned: Scoping a tool down to one honest job makes it more trustworthy — and somehow more useful.

projects.name: DCA Analysis
projects.description: Dollar Cost Averaging, replayed on real Bitcoin prices — drag the start date and watch the average cost move.

caseStudy.why: Dollar-cost averaging is easy to preach and hard to picture. DCA Analysis replays a real DCA plan against Bitcoin's own price history and shows exactly what would have happened.
highlights: Replays DCA schedules against real historical prices
Drag the start date and watch the average cost move
Honest accounting: totals, cost basis, and the rough patches too
caseStudy.learned: A replay of history persuades people in a way projections never do.

projects.name: POGO Metrics
projects.description: Turn your official Niantic Pokémon GO data export into a private, in-browser dashboard of your trainer journey.

caseStudy.why: Niantic will email you every scrap of data Pokémon GO holds on you — as a pile of raw files nobody can read. POGO Metrics turns that export into a dashboard of your trainer journey, without the data ever leaving your browser.
highlights: Parses the official Niantic data export entirely client-side — nothing is uploaded
Distills years of gameplay into charts you can actually explore
Zero backend: static hosting, no accounts, no tracking
caseStudy.learned: Privacy as a feature — processing a sensitive export in the browser removes the scariest part of every “upload your data” tool.

projects.name: ABC Applied Analysis
projects.description: ASU analytics capstone: building Buckeye's Pokémon GO community from scratch, then measuring which events and formats actually brought players out.

caseStudy.why: Buckeye, Arizona had no organized Pokémon GO community. The capstone for ASU's Applied Business Data Analytics certificate was to build one — and use the check-in data to find out what worked.
highlights: Scheduled events as soon as they were announced instead of 1–3 days out, so families could plan
Standardized event posts (via Sundance DeGen) and a single central raid meeting point
Check-in analysis found Gigantamax events drew the most players — 31 on average
caseStudy.learned: Community building is an operations problem: consistency and lead time beat hype.

projects.name: POGO Trainer Model
projects.description: Started as a linear regression in a notebook; became an interactive study of 883 trainers across two eras of the level cap — including where the first model went wrong.

caseStudy.why: Can trainer level predict battles won, distance walked and Pokémon caught? One friends list, recorded under the old level-50 cap and again under the new cap of 80, gave a real dataset to find out.
highlights: 390 trainers under the cap-50 era, 493 under cap-80
Explorer to switch fits (linear, log-linear, median) and outlier handling and watch the model move
A 'model report card' grading the original regression against alternatives — and reality
caseStudy.learned: My first model hit a ceiling at level 50. Explaining why it failed turned out to be the most interesting finding.

projects.name: Silph Relay
projects.description: A $0/month Discord relay — six Pokémon X accounts pushed to two channels in under a minute, with an analytics dashboard.

caseStudy.why: Six Pokémon accounts post into a Discord relay that costs $0/month to run — no X API, no server. The dashboard answers the operational questions: how often does each feed post, and how fast does a post land?
highlights: GitHub Actions plus a free cron trigger — no server, no paid API
Tracks post frequency and delivery latency per feed
Static analytics dashboard on the same $0 footprint
caseStudy.learned: Even a hobby bot is worth measuring. Tracking its delay showed exactly what to speed up.

projects.name: Sundance DeGen
projects.description: Turn a month's Pokémon GO schedule into copy-ready Campfire meetup posts — artwork, catch CP, and shiny status filled in.

caseStudy.why: Writing Campfire meetup posts for a month of Pokémon GO events is repetitive community work. DeGen turns the schedule into copy-ready posts — artwork, catch CP, and shiny status filled in automatically.
highlights: Generates a month of meetup posts from a markdown schedule
Auto-fills artwork, catch CP, and shiny availability
Output formatted and ready to paste into Campfire
caseStudy.learned: Automating the tedious parts of running a community leaves more energy for the fun parts.

projects.name: MickeyDeez Map
projects.description: A crowdsourced map of Phoenix's Pokémon GO–sponsored McDonald's — 31 stops, each verified as an active raid Gym.

caseStudy.why: Phoenix’s McDonald’s-sponsored PokéStops were scattered folklore. This map makes them a verified dataset: 31 stops, each confirmed as an active raid Gym.
highlights: Interactive Leaflet map of all 31 sponsored locations
Every stop community-verified as an active raid Gym
Geocoded for route planning, built with Python and Folium
caseStudy.learned: A small, verified dataset beats a big, stale one — curation is the product.

projects.name: Galaxy Royale
projects.description: A mobile 4X where one human fights 249 simulated commanders in a 2500×2500-tile galaxy that keeps living while you sleep.

caseStudy.why: A research question: could a mobile 4X go from a blank folder to running on my own iPhone, designed and redesigned conversationally with an AI coding assistant? The answer was yes — three times over.
highlights: 249 AI commanders that play by the same rules you do
One persistent galaxy that simulates a live MMO server, single-player
Three incarnations: a TypeScript prototype, an online Unity build, and this final form

projects.name: Smalltown Hustle
projects.description: A life-sim RPG in the spirit of the Flash era: one small city, a 24-hour day, and ambitions honest work can't afford.

caseStudy.why: An original take on the Flash-era life RPGs, built so the whole economy can be tuned without touching code.
highlights: Every tunable number — jobs, prices, rates — lives in one economy file
Seeded RNG that rolls at sleep, so reloading can't reroll the day
Work, study, gamble or smuggle your way to one of several endings

projects.name: The Food Banker
projects.description: An operations sim about how a food bank moves food, money, people and data — and how it grows from one warehouse to a network.

caseStudy.why: The day job, as a game: a cutaway food bank where every room only works with volunteers in it.
highlights: Rooms from the dock to the pickup lane that run continuously
Grows from a warehouse to a distribution center, storefront and rural sites
Seasons and a yearly challenge in its legacy years

projects.name: Drafter
projects.description: A household planner for web and iPhone. Tasks, calendar, meals, groceries, money, people and a daily journal live in one place, and AI assistants can help plan the week.

caseStudy.why: Running a home is spread across a dozen apps: a calendar here, a grocery list there, notes everywhere. Drafter puts it all in one place, shared with the household and working offline, so planning the week takes one look instead of six.
highlights: Plan the week in one view: tasks, calendar events and meals side by side, with Google and Outlook calendars synced in
A grocery list, budget, contacts, places, wardrobe and a daily journal sit next to the plan, so nothing gets lost in another app
Shared with the household and works offline, then syncs when you're back online
An MCP server with about 47 tools lets AI assistants like Claude read and update your plan, from adding a task to drafting the week's meals, only with the permissions you give them
Ask questions in plain English across your own records, like what's due this week or when you last saw someone
caseStudy.learned: When two devices change the same thing offline, ask which version to keep instead of quietly overwriting one.

projects.name: RemoteJoy Audio
projects.description: Stream a real PSP's screen and game audio to a Mac over one USB cable — the first PSP screen-streamer to carry audio.

caseStudy.why: Every PSP streaming tool carried video only; the standard advice was a 3.5 mm cable into a capture card. This captures the audio inside the PSP and sends it down the same USB cable.
highlights: Kernel plugin hooks the PSP's audio output calls and mixes all 8 hardware channels at the right levels
Video and audio multiplexed over USB bulk transfers
libretro client in RetroArch, native on Apple Silicon
caseStudy.learned: Recording one sound channel only gives you part of the music. Mixing every channel together in real time is what makes it sound right.

projects.name: Empire Earth on macOS
projects.description: Run your own GOG copy of Empire Earth Gold on an Apple Silicon Mac, full screen, with free tools — and armies of up to 10,000 units.

caseStudy.why: A 2001 classic, playable on a modern Mac without CrossOver or Parallels.
highlights: Full screen at native resolution, Cmd+Tab, and notch-aware layouts
~130 FPS in thousand-unit battles on an M2 Pro, with game maths moved to modern CPU instructions
Unit limit raised to 10,000, with drag-select that takes the whole box

projects.name: I-Combinator
projects.description: Combine images side by side or stacked, without cropping — drag, drop, reorder, and export in your browser.

caseStudy.why: Combining screenshots usually means opening an image editor for a ten-second job. I-Combinator does side-by-side or stacked combos in the browser — drag, drop, reorder, export.
highlights: Canvas-based compositing with no cropping surprises
Drag-and-drop ordering with instant preview
Everything stays local — images never leave the machine
caseStudy.learned: The browser alone is enough for a real image tool. The hard part is making the layout behave the way people expect.

projects.name: Edge as Chrome
projects.description: An Edge extension that makes Edge identify as Chrome on the sites you choose, so 'unsupported browser' messages go away.

caseStudy.why: Some sites refuse Edge for no reason other than its name.
highlights: Rewrites the User-Agent header, Sec-CH-UA client hints and navigator values
Per-site: every other site still sees normal Edge
One click to turn it on for the current site

projects.name: HomeTech Offer Analysis
projects.description: Exploratory analysis of customer device ownership — and which probing questions actually lead to protection-plan sales.

caseStudy.why: Does the device a customer asks about predict the other devices they own — and which questions turn that into a protection-plan sale?
highlights: EDA on a synthetic customer dataset
Device-ownership profiles, from customers with many devices to those with none
Compared probing questions by conversion rate
